videos.title: AI Risk, Superintelligence & The Fight Ahead — A Deep Dive with Liv Boeree | For Humanity #74
videos.description: 📢Take Action on AI Risk → http://www.safe.ai/act 💚Stand with Us this Giving Tuesday  → https://www.every.org/guardrailnow  In this episode of For Humanity, John Sherman sits down with @LivBoeree  — poker champion, systems thinker, and longtime AI risk advocate — for a wide-ranging conversation about the forces shaping advanced AI. Liv unpacks why people struggle to grasp superintelligence risk, how incentives and competition distort the entire ecosystem, and why cultural dynamics — from gender to surveillance to social media addiction — matter more than most realize.  Timestamp⏳ 0:01 – Intro 0:37 – Liv’s background and current view of the AI moment 3:21 – How public awareness of AI risk is shifting 6:19 – Why superintelligence is still a hard idea for many 8:03 – Conscious vs. non-conscious systems causing harm 9:49 – The impact of the book rollout and public reactions 11:27 – The Magnus Carlsen metaphor on superintelligence 13:16 – How to talk about near-term vs long-term risks 17:12 – Why job loss, addiction, and misalignment matter 20:27 – The economy as a form of “misaligned intelligence” 23:13 – Gender imbalance in AI and why it matters 27:21 – How to engage mothers and parents on AI issues 30:39 – Would female leadership change AI incentives? 35:12 – Liv’s journey into professional poker 41:00 – Math vs psychology: what makes a great poker player 44:28 – Bringing poker skills into AI risk 48:45 – Mindset: staying grounded in an age of existential risk 52:38 – If Liv were president: what she’d do about AI 58:26 – The under-discussed risk: AI-enabled surveillance 1:02:03 – Why “slow down” isn’t the whole answer 1:07:30 – AI for medicine vs AI for profit 1:10:18 – What gives Liv hope 1:13:09 – Closing  They also explore what it feels like to work on existential risk, the psychological toll of doomscrolling, and why grounding practices, intuition, and community matter in a moment where technology is moving faster than society can adapt. The result is a clear, thoughtful, and unexpectedly hopeful look at what’s coming — and what’s still within our control.  If you want a deeper understanding of how AI intersects with power, coordination, human behavior, and risk, this conversation is essential.  🔎 They explore:  • The real risks emerging from today’s AI systems — and what’s coming next  • Why superintelligence remains so misunderstood by the public  • How incentives, competition, and culture push AI development off-course  • What poker and game theory reveal about deception, risk, and strategic thinking  • How women, intuition, and “mama bear energy” could reshape the AI safety movement  👉 Follow More of Liv's Work: YouTube - @LivBoeree  Website - https://www.livboeree.com/  🎙️ About For Humanity A podcast from the AI Risk Network, hosted by John Sherman, making AI extinction risk kitchen-table conversation on every street.  📺 Subscribe for weekly conversations on how we can confront the AI extinction threat.  #AISafety #AIAlignment #ForHumanityPodcast #AIRisk #FutureOfAI #AIandWarfare #AutonomousWeapons #AIEthics #TechForGood #ArtificialIntelligence

videos.title: Teaching kids how to use AI responsibly
videos.description: Are you worried your teen is spending more time with a chatbot than with real friends?  On this episode, we spoke with @SSMHC child/adolescent psychiatrists Dr. Jeremy Chapman and Dr. Ashvin Sood to learn how AI shows up in teens’ social lives and schoolwork, and how parents can respond with clarity instead of panic. Together we map out a simple framework: curiosity first, judgment last, and functionality as the North Star for family decisions.   We explored why adolescence depends on honest, sometimes uncomfortable feedback — the kind you don’t get when a bot always agrees. You’ll hear practical ways to ask better questions about prompts, privacy, and purpose:   • "What do you ask your chatbot?" • "How does it make you feel afterward?" • "Did it help you prepare for a real conversation, or replace one?"  Both clinicians outlined red flags of AI overuse (falling grades, dropped activities, hostility when access is limited, and late‑night screen time pushing sleep off a cliff) and they offer calm, early interventions that will rebuild routines without power struggles.   We also got specific about safety in a world where parental controls lag behind fast‑moving features. You’ll learn why young people should avoid using AI for companionship, how to set clear boundaries on data-sharing, and how to implement reasonable guardrails like teaching teens to verify information and keep real relationships at the center.   By the end of the episode, you’ll have conversation scripts, monitoring cues, and a balanced mindset to make AI a helpful coach rather than a stand‑in for human connection.   📍 *Chapters:* 00:00 - Advice for parents with AI 00:59 - Old lessons for new tech 03:49 - Why child psychiatrists must 'speak AI' 05:24 - Teens and chatbots 07:02 - The cost of endless validation 09:12 - Parental controls are the new Wild West 10:17 - Curiosity over judgment at home 11:44 - Spotting overuse and AI dependency 13:29 - Know your child’s baseline and red flags 15:15 - When chatbots overpraise 16:01 - Practical AI guardrails for home 18:15 - Privacy vs. Secrets   *aiEDU: The AI Education Project* • https://aiEDU.org • https://linkedin.com/company/aiedu  *Dr. Aliza Pressman* • https://draliza.com • https://linkedin.com/in/aliza-pressman-ph-d-279b7125/

videos.title: Being citizens in an AI-powered world
videos.description: AI can sound human, but it isn’t — and that difference changes how we teach, parent, and prepare kids for a future shaped by AI.   On this episode, we dive into AI readiness: the blend of skills, ethics, and technical insight that young people need to question, adapt, and lead in an AI-powered world.  We sit down with Philip Colligan of the @RaspberryPiFoundation to unpack layered AI literacy, including what students should know about data, large language models, bias, and the social impact of automation. He shares how Experience AI (co-created with @googledeepmind)  equips teachers with free classroom resources so every student can get hands-on practice with training AI models, diagnosing bias, and interpreting results. From “tomato vs. apple” misclassification to image-generation blind spots, Phil shows how simple activities can spark important conversations about fairness, accuracy, and accountability.   We also hear from Kenyan teacher Mr. Monyancha Isena, whose students crowd around limited computers yet light up as they test AI models and ask why accuracy never hits 100%. Their curiosity illustrates a bigger point of how access and equity determine who benefits from AI.   If you’re a parent, teacher, or curious listener, you’ll leave with concrete ideas on how to build AI-ready habits: teach students how AI systems learn, demonstrate model bias through classroom activities, keep privacy guardrails in place, and emphasize student agency in using AI technology.   📍 *Chapters:* 00:00 - What is AI readiness? 02:09 - The mission of Raspberry Pi 03:04 - Layers of AI literacy 04:23 - Why hands-on learning matters 05:48 - The global curriculum of Experience AI 07:43 - Teaching about AI models and bias 09:10 - Coding still matters in AI 10:22 - Safety, privacy, and anthropomorphism 12:57 - How a Kenyan classroom teaches AI literacy 16:54 - Resource gaps in learning about AI   *aiEDU: The AI Education Project* • https://aiEDU.org • https://linkedin.com/company/aiedu  *Dr. Aliza Pressman* • https://draliza.com • https://linkedin.com/in/aliza-pressman-ph-d-279b7125/

videos.title: Chain of Thought | Introducing SWE-Bench Pro
videos.description: Introducing SWE-Bench Pro. In this episode of Chain of Thought,  @Scale_AI 's  Brad Kenstler (Head of Agent Capabilities and Environments) and Chetan Rane (Head of Product, Agents) sit down with Edwin Pan (Product Manager) and Jeff Da (ML Research Scientist) to deep dive Scale's latest. benchmark, SWE-Bench Pro.   SWE-Bench Pro is a benchmark designed to provide a rigorous and realistic evaluation of AI agents for software engineering. It was developed to address several limitations in existing benchmarks by tackling four key challenges: Data Contamination, Limited Task Diversity, Oversimplified Problems,  and Unreliable and Irreproducible Testing.  SWE-Bench Pro addresses these gaps by sourcing tasks from diverse and complex codebases, including consumer applications, B2B services, and developer tools. To reduce contamination risk, the public and held-out OSS subsets use strong copyleft licenses (e.g., GPL). The commercial subset consists of private, proprietary codebases from startup partners. videos.title: Answering parents' questions about AI
videos.description: Are you worried your kids might let AI do their thinking for them?   On this episode, Alex and Dr. Aliza dig into the questions parents ask most and share a practical roadmap for raising curious, confident, and discerning kids who can use AI without losing their edge. Whether it's developing everyday habits to build critical thinking or setting clear boundaries for schoolwork, we show how to help your kids become AI ready — fluent with AI tools, appropriately skeptical, and proud of their human advantage.   We start by unpacking what AI readiness looks like at home and in class:  • Using AI as a tutor, not a shortcut • Asking for hints and feedback instead of final answers • Testing understanding by explaining concepts in their own words.   From there, the conversation shifts to AI ethics around cheating and why expectations should be set by teachers up front. Cheating isn’t new, but trust matters and class assignments should clarify when AI is and isn't welcome.   We also look at AI-generated misinformation and deepfakes. For this, we offer simple, repeatable checks that kids can use right away:  • Pause, ask what would make this true. • Verify the info through a second source. • Look for who benefits if you believe it.  Finally, we talk timing and development: when to introduce AI, how to avoid leapfrogging core skills, and why creative success still depends on taste and craft. You can’t speed-run taste — hours of practice, feedback, and iteration teach judgment that AI can’t replace.   📍 *Chapters:* 00:00 - Parents' questions and concerns about AI 01:22 - What 'AI readiness' really means 03:38 - Building critical thinking without AI 04:44 - AI ethics, cheating, and classroom norms 08:21 - Educators' perspective on AI tools and trust 10:55 - Spotting deepfakes and AI-generated misinformation 13:45 - Teach skepticism, not cynicism. 15:56 - When to introduce AI in learning 17:46 - Taste, craft, and productive struggle 19:05 - 'Learning to learn' as the goal   *aiEDU: The AI Education Project* • https://aiEDU.org • https://linkedin.com/company/aiedu  *Dr. Aliza Pressman* • https://draliza.com • https://linkedin.com/in/aliza-pressman-ph-d-279b7125/

The Udacity Institute of AI & Technology is a member college of Woolf that provides learners with a path to a fully online master’s program. Woolf is an accredited higher education institution recognized in 60+ countries. The degree consists of 2,250 credit hours, or the equivalent of about 12 Udacity Nanodegree programs and capstone project. There are 7 required Nanodegree programs and students can earn the remainder of their credits through electives. This provides a structured pathway combining project-based, industry-aligned coursework with academic recognition.  Who can apply to this degree program?  Anyone with an undergraduate degree is eligible to apply. If you don’t have a degree, you may still be eligible through the Performance-Based Admission (PBA) pathway.  Am I required to pay the full program fee of $5000?  No. Getting started simply requires you to pay the enrollment fee of $199 USD and be a Udacity subscriber which starts at $249 USD a month. The estimated cost of $5000 assumes it takes 19-months to finish the full program at $249/month. However, you can cancel at anytime.
